result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers propose a 3×4 grid of small charts, one per branch, with a shared scale and Dunmere highlighted in a grayscale-safe way. A is tighter and keeps the other eleven panels quieter. B adds padding, such as the no-interactivity point, an unexplained reference to 'the color guidance', and an average line in every panel, which adds noise. On the case where branch sizes differ widely, both give an honest choice between scales, but neither mentions a log scale. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend a 3×4 small-multiples grid with a shared scale, direct branch labels, Dunmere picked out in an accent colour with a July closure marker, and grayscale-safe printing. B wins narrowly. It is tighter and has useful extras for the data: annual totals in each panel header, which keep comparisons honest if scales differ; a hollow point for a partly closed July; and an optional 2024 baseline for Dunmere. A pads with less relevant points, such as the note on interactivity and an unexplained appeal to 'color guidance', and the average line it adds to every panel makes the other eleven less quiet.
